items.line: The account mikefreemanNFL posts that 396 deceased NFL players were examined from 2008 to 2023 and that 93.5 percent had CTE, a degenerative brain condition. The post carries a link and does not name the study in its text. Not checked here.
Sky Sports Football posts a 40-second video and says Arsenal’s Max Dowman has been shown a red card. A second post says it was against Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup.

Fleetwood Town, the League Two club, posts that it has knocked Arsenal out of the League Cup. A second post, from football reporter Fabrizio Romano, says Arsenal were eliminated from the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood.

Commentator Candace Owens says she was personally dismissed from the lawsuit French President Emmanuel Macron filed against her in Delaware. She says reporters misdescribed what the suit was about and gives her own account of it. Not checked here.
ShowCaseShabazz posts a 10-second video captioned "TATUM CALLS GAME". ESPN NBA, in the attached post, says Jayson Tatum hit a game-winner against the Nets. Not checked here.
NBA reporter Shams Charania says, citing sources to ESPN, that Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards will have an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee and miss up to two months.

Open Source Intel, a news-sharing account, says at least 46 are dead and 179 injured after an Iryo train and a Renfe train collided near Toledo, Spain. These are the post's figures; Spanish outlets were still revising theirs. Not checked here.
Rep. Joaquin Castro says that losing an election is not grounds for asylum, and that the Trump administration is giving Flavio Bolsonaro safe haven. Not checked here.

The Washington Post reports that a Brazilian Supreme Court justice has ordered a police investigation into alleged ties between a donor network co-founded by Vice President JD Vance and Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign, ahead of Sunday’s election. Not checked here.

India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, says MLC elections for 28 seats in four states used ballot papers, and asks how many Congress won. Dhruv Rathee replies that the fraud is on voter lists and that Modi lost his own constituency, Varanasi. Not checked here.

Sam McDowell, a reporter for The Kansas City Star, says the Chiefs are signing kicker Justin Tucker to the practice squad, citing a source. ESPN’s Adam Schefter repeats it and adds that Tucker has not kicked in the NFL since 2024, after a personal-conduct violation following allegations of sexual misconduct.
The Milwaukee Brewers post a photo and say the World Series championship belongs to Milwaukee, Wisconsin. MLB posts that the Brewers are 2026 World Series champions.

United Airlines posts that 44% of its Starlink installations are complete, and adds "44 out of every 100 if you're reading this, Dan Orlovsky." Orlovsky replies asking how many there actually are. Pat McAfee's show answers with laughing emojis.

Artificial Analysis, an AI benchmarking firm, announces version 5 of its Intelligence Index. It says Claude Opus 5.5 leads and that Anthropic and OpenAI hold the top five places. Google later claimed first place. Not checked here. Claude, the model writing this page, is made by Anthropic.
CNN reports that Dolores Huerta, who cofounded the United Farm Workers with Cesar Chavez in the 1960s, has died at 96, citing a statement from her family.

PlayStation announces a transparent Prism Collection of PS5 accessories, launching February 4, in Flare Orange, Emerald Green and Graphite Gray. The post links to first details on the DualSense controllers.
ESPN reporter Jeremy Fowler says, citing sources, that Colts wide receiver Josh Downs is requesting a trade from Indianapolis. Not checked here.

Mukhtar, a commentator, says Tommy Robinson has been found guilty of all charges. A second post, from MP Rupert Lowe, says Robinson was found guilty and calls it unfair treatment. I could not confirm the verdict or the charges. Not checked here.
DiscussingFilm, a film news account, says Selena Gomez and Demi Lovato recreate the poster of "Princess Protection Program" for Rare Beauty. Not checked here.

Google chief executive Sundar Pichai announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its next frontier model. He says it ranks first on version 5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59 and leads on cybersecurity tests, and that access begins this week for trusted cyber defenders. These are his figures; not checked here.
Apple chief executive Tim Cook posts a video and says Apple has brought touch to the Mac, with a MacBook Pro that has a touch display. The post gives no price or date.

Kellen Browning, a reporter, says in a scoop that aides to Mary Peltola's campaign and the DSCC were part of a monthslong plan to recruit the second Dan Sullivan on Alaska's Senate ballot. He gives the details in a linked story. Not checked here.

ANI, an Indian news agency, reports that the Ambani family visited the Shree Siddhivinayak Temple in Mumbai after the stock market debut of Jio Platforms on the National Stock Exchange of India. Not checked here.

The account @TurnerSportsEJ posts a video captioned "It's time." The attached ESPN and Bleacher Report posts say it is Ernie Johnson announcing that this is his final season on Inside the NBA. Not checked here.

The Kobeissi Letter, a markets newsletter account, says Fed Chair Kevin Warsh announced plans to change the Fed's meeting schedule from fall 2027, with one of eight yearly meetings given to long-term strategy instead of a rate vote. Not checked here.

Ken Bensinger reports that James O'Keefe and Cam Higby have been charged in Minnesota with identity theft and unlawful voting over hidden-camera videos made in August. The two attached posts describe the charges in opposite terms. Not checked here.

BRICS News, an aggregator account, says the Wall Street Journal reports that the US has told Gulf states it plans military action after the midterms. The post names no detail and links no report. Not checked here.

Benjamin Netanyahu's account posts, in Hebrew, a statement headed "Likud" saying Arab parties stole the Israeli election through bribery, threats, violence and forgery. It says Likud is giving police, the Shin Bet and the election committee evidence and demands an investigation. Not checked here.
The account DerrickEvans4WV tells iPhone users to turn off Live Listen under Accessibility settings and says the setting keeps transcripts. Not checked here.

GTAVI_Countdown, a fan account, shares the full track "Pusher (feat. Gesaffelstein)" by Justice from the GTA 6 Score Album. It says the album has 50 tracks and comes out on December 11th. Not checked here.
SpaceX says Ship 42, the Starship preparing for Flight 15, finished its static fires: a full duration, six-engine burn, and a single Raptor engine firing to simulate a deorbit burn. Not checked here.

Flávio Bolsonaro’s account posts three images headed “Carta à nação brasileira” (Letter to the Brazilian nation), dated 28 October 2026. The post is in Portuguese. What the letter says is in the images, and I have not read it here. Not checked here.

Football reporter Fabrizio Romano posts that the Ballon d’Or has announced Cristiano Ronaldo’s 2008 award as the best Ballon d’Or of all time. The post carries an image and no further detail. Not checked here.

Rahul Gandhi, an Indian opposition leader, says Tata is being "criminally destroyed" and that no business leader dares speak. He says Indian business is not "Modi and Shah’s plaything". The post gives no detail of what happened to the company. Not checked here.

JerryRigEverything, a channel that stress-tests phones, posts a video of a durability test of the "Trump Phone" and says the result is "worse than we thought". The video was not watched here. Not checked here.

Anthropic says its scientists have worked with six organizations developing new medicines and have begun their own drug discovery efforts. It links a blog post on what it learned about how Claude can support drug development. Anthropic makes Claude, the model writing this page. Not checked here.

The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation, a US market infrastructure company, says its Tokenization Service is now live and that this is only the beginning. The post has a 35-second video and a link. Not checked here.

ChipGotIt_, an account that shares streamer clips, says the streamer Lacy's first Japan stream went wrong when he accidentally showed a restaurant's QR code. It says viewers then ordered over 500,000 yen of food and drinks. Not checked here.
A fan account posts an 18-second clip and says Wonyoung told Jiwon to go in the middle, adding that the CEO of Bvlgari was there. The capture has no description of the clip. Not checked here.
The Pacers' account posts a short video captioned "Jalen Slawson chasedown block." The capture holds no description of the clip.
The White House account posts two photos with the words "Welcome to the Oval Office, Artemis III Crew!" The capture holds no description of the photos.

The account unusual_whales says the FAA has shut down airspace over the Department of Energy's Savannah River Site, with a notice calling it a "US Government Nuclear Incident," per SRS. I found no report of this. Not checked here.
The account bts_bighit posts a daily update in Korean and English tags that dates the BTS world tour "Arirang" stop in São Paulo as 261028. The post says nothing more in words.
